title: Common definitions shared by all device-toolkit contracts
description: Every other schema in this folder $refs into this file. Nothing here is a wire format by itself.

uuid.description: RFC 4122 UUID. Operation/Audit ids are UUIDv4; never reused across restarts.

deviceId.description: Internal, non-sensitive device identity. Derived from transport identity + a local salt, so it is stable per machine but cannot be reversed into a serial.

isoTimestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC with 'Z'. Local time is never stored in contracts.

transportKind.description: How the device is reached. A single physical device can expose several transports at once; each is a separate handle.

connectionState.description: Transport-level state as reported by the transport, not an interpretation of device health.

availability.description: Capability/field availability. 'Unknown' means not yet probed; 'NotReported' means the protocol answered but carried no value.

confidence.description: How much to trust a value: High = read directly from a documented source; Medium = parsed with a heuristic or an OEM-specific property; Low = inferred.

evidenceSource.description: Where a value came from. 'Derived' means computed from other fields and must never be presented as read from the device.

redactionPolicy.description: How an identity field is stored in audits. Raw serials never appear in logs.

problemCode.description: The closed set of machine-readable failure codes. Every Result carries exactly one. Human text is a separate field and never parsed by callers.

recoverability.description: What the caller may do next. 'RetryAfterReconcile' forbids automatic retry: the operation may already have taken effect.

operationState.description: Terminal states are Succeeded, Partial, Failed, Cancelled. OutcomeUnknown and NeedsReconciliation are NOT terminal: they require a reconcile step before any retry.

impactLevel.description: Drives the approval requirement. Destructive operations are not implemented in V1.

byteSize.description: Bytes. Never a formatted string ('1.2 GB') in a contract.

androidPath.description: Absolute POSIX path on the device. '..' segments are rejected by the policy layer, not by the schema.

windowsPath.description: Absolute Windows path. The policy layer additionally rejects UNC paths, device paths (\\.\), and reparse-point escapes.

scopeDigest.description: SHA-256 over the canonical (sorted-key, UTF-8, no-whitespace) JSON of the approved Plan. If the plan changes by one byte, the token no longer matches. This is what makes approval non-transferable.

approvedBy.description: Which surface requested the approval. Recorded for audit; it does not grant more trust.
